problem_type: credential persistence and catalog publication invariant regression
symptom: A newly saved onboarding API credential could fall back to plaintext when Electron safeStorage was unavailable; legacy plaintext could still be resolved by runtime execution and health probes; staged, failed, or wrong-mode adapter models could appear in production lists; mode-specific custom calls could be published for unsupported sibling modes; and an unverified credential re-save could combine a replacement model contract with the previously published mapping.
direct_cause: The shared API-key writer returned enc=plain instead of failing and the shared execution decryptor returned legacy plaintext; custom-call publication expanded generic or unparseable mode scripts to every task in a billing kind, while malformed explicit capability contracts fell through to identity-based archetypes and runtime generic scripts; publication consumers used divergent enabled/adapter checks without exact task modes; register and catalog commit overwrote active contract fields before promotion; and multi-model manual onboarding repeated independent credential/catalog transactions.
class_root: Credential readiness, active model contracts, and executable task modes were represented by permissive mutable fields at multiple consumers instead of being derived and committed at shared secure-storage, publication-DTO, promotion, and catalog-transaction boundaries.
affected_population: Users creating or editing an authenticated model connection on a host where Electron safeStorage is unavailable or encryption fails
Users with legacy enc=plain or pre-encoding API-key records entering a new adapter authentication run
Users viewing MCP or normal model pickers while an onboarding model is staged, unverified, partially verified, or failed
entry_points: CatalogMutation.upsertApiKey used by manual onboarding and provider-adapter register/stage writes
deriveModelListing for nomi_list_models and modelCatalogCache for normal renderer pickers
internal_only_reason: This change enforces Nomi's approved internal persistence and promotion invariants. External provider or protocol behavior cannot decide whether local plaintext storage is acceptable or whether Nomi publishes an unverified catalog row.
invariants: Every new or edited authenticated credential is encrypted through safeStorage or the transaction throws before catalog persistence; thrown errors never contain the submitted secret.
Legacy plaintext remains structurally recognizable as needs_resave but is not credential-ready for a new authentication run.
The shared execution credential resolver returns plaintext only for decryptable safeStorage records; legacy material never reaches an execution request, health probe, error, or log.
Only verified executable modes enable new mappings and models; vendor enabled state is derived from at least one verified or preserved active executable model.
Unverified registration or credential re-save cannot replace any field of an already-published model contract; a verified promotion is the contract switch boundary.

An unverified endpoint, auth, header, provider-kind, or credential replacement is stored under a stable isolated candidate vendor identity; failure leaves the active shared vendor byte-identical and promotion switches only verified target models while preserving siblings.
Renderer model DTOs carry published and exact publishedModes derived in Electron from active revisions, custom calls, enabled mappings, or the text-only legacy path.
A legacy generic custom-call script publishes only the billing kind's minimal default task mode, while mode-specific scripts publish only task kinds proven by their explicit capability contract.

The shared capability manifest treats any present explicit contract as authoritative: all structural, kind, task, default, and uniqueness checks must pass, otherwise publication and runtime dispatch expose zero modes without built-in or generic fallback.
A multi-model manual onboarding save validates every candidate first, encrypts once per vendor, and commits every vendor/model/mapping change in one catalog mutation.
An enabled model with an existing custom-call, executable mapping, or active adapter revision remains published during credential re-save or a failed repair.

Unverified staged rows stay visible in settings metadata but are excluded from nomi_list_models and normal pickers, while legacy catalog rows and models with a preserved active revision remain available.
Production node and batch pickers pass the current executable task mode through the catalog cache, and batch model changes apply only to nodes in the same task-mode group.
migration: Existing enc=plain and encoding-absent records remain in place and are reported as needs_resave so the UI can request an explicit credential re-save. Their plaintext is not returned by the execution decryptor, sent to providers, silently re-encrypted, or admitted to a new certification run. Only legacy text models retain the historical adapter-less direct path; media models require an active revision, enabled executable mapping, or conservatively published custom call. An adapter model with an activeRevision remains published while a repair run is staged or fails. Replacing a published connection creates a stable isolated candidate vendor row; successful verified promotion disables only the replaced source model and its exact mappings, while failed candidates leave the source vendor and sibling models unchanged.
residual_risks: Legacy plaintext remains present on disk until the user explicitly re-saves or removes it; this task prevents new plaintext writes but does not destructively delete migration evidence.
Settings surfaces intentionally continue to show configured unverified rows so users can repair them; only production selection surfaces are verified-only.
Catalog rows predating adapter metadata retain compatibility only for text, whose historical direct AI SDK path is executable without a mapping.
